finding.comment: The jq filter assumes the input is a single array, but events_jsonl holds one object per line; any(.[]; …) therefore iterates each object's own values instead of the findings, so the error check misreads the input format.

files.patch:
--- a/scripts/scan.sh
+++ b/scripts/scan.sh
@@ -1,3 +1,6 @@
 # findings were collected as JSONL (one object per line):
 #   jq -c '.[]' <<<"$batch" >>"$events_jsonl"
+if ! jq -e 'any(.[]; .level == "error")' <"$events_jsonl" >/dev/null; then
+  echo "at least one error finding" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi

rationale: unslurped array consumer over a JSONL producer (M6 semantics)
